**ASTRAL — An Intelligent Multi-Domain Astronaut Health Monitoring System**

ASTRAL is a research-oriented prototype developed to explore how astronauts' health can be monitored more systematically during space missions. It brings together health indicators across seven interconnected domains: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, immune-related, neuro-ocular, behavioral, radiation exposure, and nutrition.

The platform features an interactive astronaut dashboard, individual metric analysis pages, historical trends, personalized baselines, and statistical alerts that highlight unusual changes. It also includes astronaut profiles, simulated mission scenarios, health logs, countermeasure tracking, and data-management tools.

ASTRAL addresses the challenge of monitoring multiple aspects of astronaut health in one place while recognizing that individuals may respond differently to the space environment. By comparing measurements against personal baselines and making trends easier to interpret, it explores how data-driven monitoring could support earlier investigation and more informed decisions.

This is important because maintaining astronauts' health and performance is essential for safe, successful, and increasingly long-duration space missions. ASTRAL aims to contribute to the exploration of more integrated and personalized approaches to space-health monitoring.
details:
ASTRAL — Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring

Project Details

ASTRAL is an interactive research prototype designed to explore a more integrated approach to astronaut health monitoring during space missions. Its central idea is that astronaut health should not be viewed as a collection of isolated measurements, but as an interconnected system in which changes across different health domains may provide valuable context.

What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRAL organizes health indicators across seven domains: cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, immune-related, neuro-ocular, behavioral, radiation exposure, and nutrition.

Users can explore an astronaut dashboard, select individual health metrics, review historical trends, record observations, and compare available measurements against personalized baselines. The platform incorporates statistical methods such as the median and median absolute deviation (MAD) to identify deviations from an individual's historical patterns. Its explainable alerts are intended to highlight observations that may deserve further investigation rather than provide medical diagnoses.

ASTRAL also includes astronaut profiles, simulated mission scenarios, health logs, countermeasure tracking, data visualization, and data-management features. It distinguishes simulated information from manually entered observations to make data provenance more transparent.

What are its benefits?

The main benefit is bringing multiple dimensions of astronaut health into one organized interface. Instead of examining each indicator independently, users can explore trends across different domains and understand how observations compare with individual baselines.

Personalized baselines are particularly relevant because astronauts may have different normal physiological patterns. Statistical deviations can therefore offer a complementary perspective to fixed thresholds, although they require further scientific validation before operational use.

What is the intended impact?

ASTRAL explores how accessible, explainable, and personalized monitoring tools could support future human space exploration. Its long-term vision is to help researchers and mission teams organize health information, investigate unusual trends, and consider astronaut wellbeing more holistically, particularly during long-duration missions where continuous access to Earth-based medical support may be limited.

Tools and technologies used

ASTRAL was developed as a web-based application using:

  • React: Building the interactive user interface and application components.
  • JavaScript (JSX): Implementing application logic and interactions.
  • Vite: Development environment and build tooling.
  • HTML and CSS: Structuring and styling the interface.
  • GitHub and GitHub Codespaces: Source-code management and cloud-based development.
  • Vercel: Deploying the application as a publicly accessible website.

The prototype uses simulated and manually entered information. It does not currently connect to live astronaut sensors or private NASA medical databases.

What makes ASTRAL creative?

ASTRAL combines personalized statistical analysis, multi-domain monitoring, and mission-oriented visualization in one platform. One of its central design choices is comparing observations with individual baselines instead of assuming that one universal threshold represents every astronaut's health.

It also brings together health monitoring and practical mission-oriented features, including logs, countermeasure tracking, historical analysis, and simulated scenarios. The aim is to make complex health information more understandable and useful for further investigation.

What factors did the team consider?

The development considered the distinctive challenges of human spaceflight, including the interconnected nature of health changes, individual physiological differences, long-duration missions, data interpretation, and the need for clear and accessible interfaces.

We also considered data reliability, transparency, privacy, and the limitations of statistical alerts. Simulated and manually entered measurements are identified as such, and the current prototype is not presented as a clinically validated diagnostic system.

ASTRAL is an early step toward exploring how intelligent, personalized health-monitoring concepts could contribute to safer and more informed human space exploration.

Also , the resources used from Nasa websites informed the research context and design considerations behind ASTRAL. The current prototype uses simulated and manually entered measurements rather than directly importing NASA datasets or accessing live astronaut medical data.

ASTRAL was developed using React, JavaScript, JSX, HTML, CSS, and Vite. GitHub Codespaces was used as the development environment, GitHub for source-code hosting, and Vercel for deployment. OpenAI ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted tool for coding support, debugging, and writing assistance; the project concept, direction, and final review were managed by the project creator. Google Slides was used to prepare the demonstration presentation.

The health measurements currently displayed in ASTRAL are simulated or manually entered for demonstration purposes. No live astronaut medical data or external health dataset is directly integrated into the current prototype.

No external images or copyrighted visual assets were intentionally incorporated into the project.
